Maya: Morning async — what I did: rolled authz parsing fix into canary (svc-token edge case). No user errors in canary logs so far.

Maya: Blocker: intermittent 502s from one egress region to our model backend, CPU for that host spikes then LB returns 502. I can reproduce ~5% of calls.

Chris: Can you paste the PR and a short log sample? I'll look at LB config.

Maya: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4782

Maya: log snippet:
```
2026-03-18T09:03:12Z gateway[svc-rt]: upstream response 502 from model-01-eu, conn-reset, backend-cpu=95%
```

deploy-bot: Canary traffic updated -> service/gateway: 10% -> 20% :rocket:

Eli: On rate limits — are we still using bucket=1000 r/s, burst=200 for org level? If backend CPU is saturated, we should lower burst window.

Sam: Ran a quick synthetic hitting /v1/generate (small prompt) against canary: p95 latency jumped from 210ms -> 480ms during the spike. curl test:
```
curl -sS -X POST https://gw.internal/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"prompt":"hi","max_tokens":8}'
```

Tess: I'll review PR #4782 and the LB rule set. Also can add a temporary rate-policy to fallback to smaller model variant on errors.

Chris: +1 to fallback policy. Can we add a short smoke check in CI that asserts /health + a 50-token generate call? If that fails, trigger rolling back canary.

Maya: OK I'll add the smoke test to the PR and drop canary to 10% if spikes continue. Token rotation note: key rotation job scheduled Tue 02:00 UTC — won't touch canary keys.

Tess: Taking PR now. If anyone sees persistent >3% error rate for 15min, ping #incidents and I'll flip region routing.

Maya: thanks — assigning reviewers @Tess @Chris. No other blockers from me.

Chris: Ack. Will follow up in-thread if I find LB misconfig.
